finding: A rollEditLog whose startLogSegment fails on all (non-required) edits dirs leaves FSEditLog in BETWEEN_LOG_SEGMENTS while the NameNode keeps running; the next rollEditLog fails Preconditions.checkState(isSegmentOpen()) in endCurrentLogSegment with IllegalStateException 'Bad state: BETWEEN_LOG_SEGMENTS'.
same_root_cause: Yes. In the buggy FSEditLog.rollEditLog (FSEditLog.java:1314-1322) endCurrentLogSegment(true) moves the state to BETWEEN_LOG_SEGMENTS, then startLogSegment (FSEditLog.java:~1382-1386) catches the JournalSet IOException and only rethrows 'Unable to start log segment 5: too few journals successfully started', leaving state unchanged and the NN alive. The next roll hits the check at FSEditLog.java:1409 (frame rollEditLog:1316 in validate-1.log). This is exactly the hunk the fix replaces: the catch block in startLogSegment now logs, closes the journalSet and calls terminate(1, msg) instead of rethrowing.
realistic: Yes. MiniDFSCluster with default config (plus valid dfs.namenode.name.dir.restore=true); the fault is an I/O failure creating the new edits_inprogress file on every edits dir (simulated by placing a directory at that path, so RandomAccessFile open fails), which is a local disk I/O failure at an I/O boundary; the rolls are ordinary rollEditLog RPC-server calls as issued by the SecondaryNameNode/standby. No reflection, no fabricated state, no direct call into the check with made-up arguments.
fixed_version: On the buggy tree plus the fix, the IllegalStateException no longer occurs (NOT_REPRODUCED, 2 attempts); the test instead fails with 'Test resulted in an unexpected exit' at MiniDFSCluster.shutdown, i.e. the first failed startLogSegment now calls terminate(), which is the fix's intended behaviour (NameNode terminates instead of continuing with no open segment).
reason: The agent's validated reproduction reaches the check through precisely the defect HDFS-14075 fixes: a failed startLogSegment during a log roll leaves the edit log with no open segment while the NameNode keeps running, so the next roll/endCurrentLogSegment fails. The trigger is a realistic disk I/O fault plus ordinary roll RPCs, and the consequence (the NN keeps running with a broken edit log and later rolls fail) matches the JIRA; the fixed version terminates the NN at the first failure instead.
